If you like, notice the slightly cooler air coming in through your nose, and the slightly warmer air leaving. Without changing it. Just notice it, once or twice, and then let it be.
[pause 4s]
If your breathing is short, or a little uneven, that's fine too. It doesn't have to be perfect. It's doing its job, one breath after another.
[pause 3s]
Now we'll travel through the body, very gently. Not to do anything. Just to say goodnight to each part, and let it settle.
If you lose track, that's okay. Pick up wherever you are, or don't pick up at all. Everything is fine.
There's no wrong way to do this. Even listening with half your attention is plenty tonight.
And if one area doesn't want to relax, leave it alone. It's allowed to stay tense. Nothing is forced tonight.
[pause 2s]
Start with your face. Your forehead, which may have been furrowed all day, in front of screens and problems. Let it widen and smooth out.
Your eyebrows, drifting a little apart. Your eyes, heavy, sinking back. Your eyelids resting, with no effort at all.
[pause 2s]
Your cheeks, which can go soft. And your jaw, which may have clenched a lot today. Let your teeth part slightly. Let your tongue rest on the floor of your mouth.
Your face often carries the effort of the day without you noticing. The polite smiles, the concentration, the jaw holding on. Tonight, it has no one to show anything to.
[pause 4s]
The back of your neck, which has carried your head all day. Your head is heavy, and tonight, it can sink completely into the pillow.
Your shoulders. They've carried so much too. Responsibilities, emergencies, other people's expectations, and your own. Let them sink, widen, and settle.
[pause 2s]
Imagine each out breath lifting a small weight off your shoulders. A project, a meeting, an expectation. You don't have to name them. They can just slide off to the side.
[pause 5s]
Your arms, heavy, resting by your sides. Your elbows. Your forearms. Your wrists.
And your hands. Hands that have typed, written, carried, held, and clicked hundreds of times today. They can open now. Palms up, if that's comfortable. Fingers soft, slightly curled.
[pause 2s]
Your hands have nothing left to hold tonight. No phone, no mouse, no mug. Maybe notice the warmth in your palms, a faint tingling in your fingertips.
[pause 4s]
Your chest, rising and falling on its own. Your heart, beating at its own pace beneath your ribs, with nothing for you to manage.
Your belly, which can let go completely. No need to hold it in, or hold it at all. It can round out, soften, spread.
The belly is often where we keep our worries. A knot, a tightness. Tonight, it can rest too, rising and falling with the breath, holding nothing back.
[pause 4s]
Your back, sinking into what's beneath you. Your upper back, between the shoulder blades, where the tension of long days so often settles. Your middle back. Your lower back.
Your pelvis, heavy, at rest. Your hips opening slightly, without effort.
[pause 4s]
Your legs. Your thighs, thick and heavy. Your knees. Your calves, which may have rushed from one meeting to the next.
Your legs have carried you through the whole day, up stairs, down hallways, from one task to the next. Let them be completely still now.
[pause 2s]
And your feet. Your ankles, your heels, the soles of your feet, your toes. All the way at the end of your body, they can rest too.
[pause 3s]
If your attention drifted during this journey, that's completely fine. Your body received what it could, even if you didn't follow every word.
[pause 4s]
There. Your whole body is resting, from head to toe. Nothing is asking you for effort now. There's nowhere to go.
[pause 3s]
Listen to this. The day is over. Whatever didn't get done will wait. What's left isn't urgent tonight. And if something truly is, tomorrow will be soon enough.
Let those words sink in slowly. You don't have to believe them right away. Just let them be here, like a warm hand on your shoulder.
[pause 3s]
Your worth doesn't depend on your productivity. Not on the number of emails sent, or the tasks checked off, or what others expect of you.
You're worth just as much tonight, motionless and drained, as on your most productive day.
[pause 3s]
Think of someone you love, as exhausted as you are tonight. You wouldn't tell them they should have done more. You'd tell them to rest. You can offer yourself the same kindness.
Maybe it feels strange to speak to yourself this way. That's okay. Just try it, quietly, tonight.
[pause 2s]
You're allowed to rest without having earned it. Rest isn't a reward you collect once everything is finished. It's a need, like drinking or eating.
Even a field is left to rest for a season. Rest is part of the cycle, not a break from it.
You can tell yourself, silently, if you like. I'm allowed to rest. Even if not everything is done. Even if others keep going.
[pause 5s]
Now my voice will grow quieter, and come a little less often. Just stay here, with your natural breath. Not looking for anything.
You can let my words reach you from far away, like a voice in another room. You don't need to hear everything. Just stay here, lying down, supported, breathing.
[pause 6s]
If thoughts drift by, things to do, worries about tomorrow, let them pass, like cars in the distance, at night.
You hear the sound of their engines, but you don't need to follow them. They continue on their way without you.
[pause 6s]
There may be sounds around you too. Rain, a neighbor, the fridge, the street. They're part of the evening. They have nothing to ask of you.
There's nothing to do with these sounds, or with these thoughts. They drift through the evening the way clouds drift across the sky. You stay grounded, resting, at ease.
[pause 6s]
You're here. Your body is supported. Your breathing happens on its own. There's nothing else to do.
[pause 5s]
Each breath is a small pause in itself. Air comes in, air goes out, and in between, there's a moment where nothing happens. You can rest in that moment.
[pause 8s]

Maybe you notice a small change. A body that feels a little heavier, a breath a little slower. Or maybe nothing in particular, just the same tiredness, lying down a little more. Both are perfectly fine.
There's no need to hold on to this feeling, or to recreate it later. It was here for you tonight, and that's enough.
[pause 3s]
Notice the surface beneath you, which hasn't moved since the beginning. It has held you this whole time, without you doing anything.
[pause 4s]
When you come out of this pause, there may still be a little evening ahead of you.
Think of one small comforting thing you could give yourself. Not an effort, not one more task. Something gentle.
A hot cup of tea in a mug you love. A shower, a bath. A soft blanket, some calm music. A message to someone who makes you feel good. Going to bed early, without guilt.
[pause 2s]
Choose one, simple and easy. Just for you.
One is enough. Tonight, gentleness matters more than anything else you could still check off your list.
[pause 3s]
You can stay lying down as long as you need. There's no rush.
If you want to get up, do it slowly. Move your fingers and toes first. Roll onto your side. Sit for a moment before you stand.
And if you'd rather stay here, or drift off to sleep, that's perfectly fine too.
Whatever you choose, you've already done something kind for yourself just by stopping for these few minutes.
[pause 3s]
One last thing, said simply. If this exhaustion has lasted for weeks, or keeps coming back, talk to a doctor or a health professional. You deserve support.
[pause 2s]
For tonight, rest. You've done enough.
[pause 4s]
